questions.q: What does a DLP policy actually control?
options: Which users are allowed to sign in to Power Automate
Which connectors can be combined together in the same flow or app
How many flows a maker is allowed to create
The performance and run speed of a flow
questions.explain: A DLP policy classifies every connector into a group and enforces which groups can be combined in a single flow or app — it's about connector combinations, not users, flow counts, or performance.

questions.q: Castlebridge's admin puts SQL Server in the Business group and Twitter in the Blocked group. What happens if a maker tries to save a flow that reads from SQL Server and posts to Twitter?
options: The flow saves normally, but an email alert is sent to the admin
The flow runs once and is then automatically deleted
The flow cannot be saved with both connectors present, because they're in different groups
Only the Twitter action is silently removed when the flow is saved
questions.explain: The core DLP rule is that a single flow can't combine connectors from two different groups. The maker is blocked from saving the flow with both connectors present, not just warned after the fact.

questions.q: What happens by default to a connector that an admin hasn't explicitly classified in a DLP policy?
options: It's automatically placed in the Blocked group
It's automatically placed in the Non-Business group
It's automatically placed in the Business group
It can't be used by anyone until it's classified
questions.explain: Non-Business is the default group. Any connector nobody has explicitly moved to Business or Blocked lands in Non-Business automatically.

questions.q: Why would Castlebridge's admin put SQL Server and Dataverse in the same connector group?
options: Because they are made by different publishers and must always be separated
Because both carry sensitive business data (shipment and finance records), and keeping them in the same group lets flows combine them while still blocking that data from reaching unrelated groups
Because only one of the two is a Premium connector
Grouping connectors by publisher is required by Power Automate
questions.explain: Connectors are grouped by data sensitivity, not publisher. Putting both sensitive-data connectors in Business allows flows to combine them with each other while still preventing that data from reaching connectors in Non-Business or Blocked.

questions.q: A DLP policy change makes an existing, already-running flow non-compliant. What happens to that flow?
options: Nothing — DLP policies only affect flows created after the policy change
The flow is permanently and immediately deleted
The flow is suspended until it's brought back into compliance
The flow keeps running exactly as before, indefinitely
questions.explain: DLP enforcement isn't limited to design time. If a policy change makes a previously valid flow non-compliant, that flow is suspended until the conflicting connectors are resolved.
